dataset_family: Clinica Universidad de Navarra Memory Unit (Pamplona, Spain): retrospective single-centre clinical cohort of 145 amnestic MCI with amyloid PET (133 also FDG-PET), Oct 2013 to Mar 2021, followed to Jan 2022; 116 with complete follow-up (75 AD converters / 41 non-converters)
method_family: Evidence type for VF-27: a baseline GDS score compared between AD converters and non-converters (ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis) in a retrospective clinical prognosis cohort. The paper's primary method is visual amyloid/FDG-PET A/N classification with diagnostic-accuracy metrics and Kaplan-Meier/HR survival. At the evidence level it is the same kind of analysis as P-647 (a baseline depression scale in converters vs non-converters)
what_it_shows: Baseline GDS did not differ between the 75 aMCI patients who converted to AD dementia and the 41 who did not (7.34 (4.62) vs 8.80 (5.88), p = 0.554); converters scored numerically lower. The comparison was made in a sample that excluded anyone with 'evidence of depression or dysthymia', although about 34% were taking antidepressants. GDS appears only in Table 1. It is not mentioned in the results text, not entered into any survival model, and never related to the PET measures. All participants have aMCI.
why: Echeveste et al., Eur J Nucl Med Mol Imaging 2025;52:3567-3577. The PDF title, DOI and content match the summaries.md block (145 aMCI, Oct 2013 to Mar 2021, sensitivity 100%/94.67%, conversion times 32.59 vs 75.07 months), although the map entry is flagged 'formula-unverified'. The block never mentions GDS. The Table 1 column header in the extract prints the order 'Total aMCI (n = 145) | Converters (n = 75) | No Converters (n = 41) | p-value', so the column assignment is printed, not inferred. Against Table A1: the study's own converter-versus-non-converter comparison of a continuous depression score is null, which bears on the conversion limb. But it is shown only in a population that excluded clinically evident depression and dysthymia. This is the same range-restriction ground round 20 applied to P-662, whose equal HAMD scores came from its exclusions: the null covers only the sub-clinical range and cannot say whether severity across the clinical range grades conversion. Hence 'partly'. The part it shows: within a depression-excluded aMCI clinical sample, baseline GDS did not separate AD converters from non-converters. It does NOT show: the first clause (all participants have aMCI), the brain-measures limb (GDS is never related to amyloid or FDG PET), or the 'although' clause. Limits: a descriptive table comparison only; the GDS version is not stated (the reference is Yesavage 1982, the 30-item scale); 29 of 145 were lost to follow-up or converted to non-AD dementia, and they are excluded from the comparison; the statistical section says all analyses were adjusted for age, sex and education, but it is unclear whether that applies to the Table 1 p values; there is no control group, and follow-up length varies. Independence: no shared sample, site or authors with P-643 (Korea University Guro) or P-647 (Shanghai Brain Health Cohort). It is also distinct from P-788 (a different Spanish centre, Zaragoza, with different authors), and it shares nothing with P-1326 or P-974. Method-family caution: its depression evidence is a baseline-scale converter comparison, like P-647's.

quotes.quote: This study retrospectively evaluated patients with a clinical diagnosis of aMCI at the Memory Unit of Clínica Universidad de Navarra from October 2013 to March 2021.

The exclusion criteria were as follows: age > 85 years, evidence of depression or dysthymia, abnormal laboratory tests, significant medical illnesses, substance abuse that could interfere with cognitive functioning
Depression was assessed using the Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS) [15].
The differences in demographic characteristics between patients with aMCI who progressed and did not progress to AD were assessed using ANOVA or the Kruskal–Wallis test, as appropriate.

(Table 1, line breaks shown as |) Total aMCI (n = 145) | Converters (n = 75) | No Converters (n = 41) | p-value | ... | GDS score | 7.14 (5.10) | 7.34 (4.62) | 8.80 (5.88) | 0.554 | Amyloid +, % | 67.59% | 95.59% | 42.85% | < 0.0001
Note: The totals for AD converters (n = 75) and non-converters (n = 41) represent patients with complete follow-up data (n = 116); 29 patients were lost to follow-up

The data in this study was drawn from a clinical setting, which can differ from those acquired from a research setting. Additionally, there was no control group, and the number of patients in each group was unequal.
